sources.title: BASE (Bielefeld Academic Search Engine)
sources.snippet:
BASE (Bielefeld Academic Search Engine) is a multi-disciplinary search engine to scholarly internet resources, created by Bielefeld University Library in Bielefeld, Germany. It is based on free and open-source software such as Apache Solr and VuFind. It harvests OAI metadata from institutional repositories and other academic digital libraries that implement the Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting (OAI-PMH), and then normalizes and indexes the data for searching. You can access the full texts of about 60% of the indexed documents for free (Open Access).

raw_results.content: Case Overview. In this case, the agent answers a fact-seeking question from the GAIA [ref] benchmark using iterative web search. The task asks for the country of an unknown-language article under DDC 633 on BASE (Bielefeld University Library) as of 2020, described as having a flag that is unique from the others. The agent issues multiple search queries to identify the relevant entry and its country of origin. Although the agent does not establish a clear evidence chain for the target article, it eventually outputs Belarus, which is not the correct answer for this instance. [...] Discussion. This case illustrates a failure mode in tool-mediated reasoning where weakly grounded signals can dominate the decision process, leading to an unsupported answer even when uncertainty is present in the agent’s intermediate reasoning. Since we know the correct answer to this GAIA task is not Belarus, revisiting the attribution results may provide insight into how the error arises. While the search results contain a BELARUSIAN entry, the content does not establish that this entry matches the task’s constraints (DDC 633, unknown language, and unique flag). At the same time, the runner-up attribution also highlights multiple reasoning steps in which the agent explicitly acknowledges uncertainty and the lack of sufficient evidence. # BASE SEARCHING ENGINE

## Overview

Germany's Bielefeld University created the robust academic search engine known as BASE (Bielefeld Academic Search Engine). It is a helpful tool for researchers, students, and academics looking for academic articles, theses, dissertations, reports, and other scholarly content because it is made to index and make scholarly resources accessible. Users can find publicly accessible research outputs from a range of sources using BASE, one of the biggest search engines for academic open access information worldwide.
